paragraphs: Absolute Zero studies whether a language model can improve its reasoning by creating its own training problems. Earlier reinforcement learning approaches with verifiable rewards can avoid labeled reasoning steps while still depending on human-curated questions and answers. This paper removes that external task-data requirement from the proposed reasoning-training process.

The resulting system, Absolute Zero Reasoner, uses one model to propose tasks and solve them. Task proposal aims to maximize the model’s learning progress, allowing the curriculum to evolve alongside its abilities. A code executor checks both the validity of proposed code-reasoning tasks and the correctness of answers, giving the learning loop feedback grounded in execution.

The authors report overall state-of-the-art performance on coding and mathematical reasoning tasks, surpassing evaluated zero-setting models trained with many human-curated examples. They also demonstrate applicability across model scales and classes. These findings support self-generated, executable tasks as a route to reasoning improvement; the external-data claim concerns this training process rather than establishing that the underlying models never underwent pretraining.
neurips-2025-absolute-zero-reinforced-se.tldr: Absolute Zero trains a model to create and solve its own executable reasoning tasks, reporting strong coding and mathematics results without external training-task data.

paragraphs: Analog in-memory computing stores trainable weights as electrical conductances in resistive devices. Electrical pulses change those conductances during training. The complication is that real devices do not respond with uniform changes: their responses can be nonlinear and asymmetric. This paper investigates how those physical response patterns alter gradient-based learning.

The theoretical analysis shows that asymmetric response functions make Analog SGD behave as though an additional penalty had been added to the intended objective. Hardware imperfections therefore affect what the training process optimizes, rather than simply adding incidental variation. The proposed residual learning algorithm addresses this effect through a bilevel optimization problem, organizing learning into two linked optimization levels.

The authors prove that their algorithm converges exactly to a critical point in the analyzed setting. A critical point is not necessarily a global optimum, so the result should retain that distinction. They also extend the approach to limited response granularity and use simulations to support the theoretical conclusions. The contribution connects device response functions directly to training behavior and a corrective learning procedure.
neurips-2025-analog-in-memory-training-o.tldr: The paper explains how asymmetric analog-device responses distort training and proposes residual learning with a proof of convergence to a critical point.

paragraphs: CosmoBench organizes cosmological simulation data into a benchmark for learning from spatial structures and formation histories. It contains 34 thousand point clouds describing dark matter halos and galaxies at three spatial scales, plus 25 thousand directed trees recording halo formation at two temporal scales. These complementary representations expose both cosmic arrangements and their development.

The benchmark supports several distinct questions: estimating cosmological parameters, predicting individual halo and galaxy velocities from collective positions, and recovering finer-resolution formation trees from coarser ones. The authors provide baselines drawn from cosmological modeling and machine learning, ranging from simple linear approaches to larger graph neural networks.

A notable empirical finding is that least-squares models using a few invariant features sometimes outperform much larger deep models that require longer training. This does not establish a universal advantage for simple methods. It shows that capturing useful structure can matter more than model size on some benchmark tasks. CosmoBench provides a shared setting for investigating how physical modeling and geometric learning can work together more effectively.
neurips-2025-cosmobench-a-multiscale-mul.tldr: CosmoBench benchmarks learning from cosmic point clouds and formation trees, finding that simple invariant-feature models sometimes outperform larger deep networks.

paragraphs: Generating a three-dimensional object from one image requires interpreting clues about shape and depth. Cue3D asks which clues modern generative systems actually use. Its contribution is a model-agnostic evaluation framework that studies these dependencies across seven methods, covering regression-based systems, approaches that use multiple views, and native 3D generators.

The framework systematically changes shading, texture, silhouettes, perspective, edges, and local continuity, then measures how the resulting 3D output quality changes. This makes it possible to examine the influence of individual cues instead of judging systems only by their overall reconstruction quality. It also reveals whether different model families respond similarly to the same visual changes.

The analysis identifies meaningful shape, rather than texture, as the driver of generalization in the evaluated setting. Geometric information, especially shading, plays a crucial role. The authors also find excessive dependence on supplied silhouettes and differing sensitivities to perspective and local continuity. These results identify concrete dependencies that can inform efforts to make single-image 3D generation more robust, interpretable, and controllable.
neurips-2025-cue3d-quantifying-the-role-.tldr: Cue3D perturbs visual cues to reveal how seven single-image 3D generators depend on shape, shading, silhouettes, and other image information.

paragraphs: Many optimization problems require selecting a permutation, such as an ordering or assignment. These discrete choices are difficult to handle with gradient-based methods. This paper introduces Birkhoff Extension, which extends real-valued objectives on permutations to doubly stochastic matrices: continuous matrices whose nonnegative entries sum to one in every row and column.

The construction uses a continuous version of Birkhoff decomposition. Its extension is computable in polynomial time and differentiable almost everywhere. Crucially, a solution in the continuous space can be efficiently rounded back to a permutation without increasing the objective value. Approximate relaxed solutions also yield approximate permutation solutions, connecting continuous optimization to the original discrete problem.

These properties allow the extension to serve as a loss for gradient-based optimization and unsupervised neural combinatorial optimization. The authors also give a procedure that can accompany existing approaches while ensuring the final solution is no worse than the starting solution. They extend the construction to a class of tree problems and present experiments supporting the theory. The guarantees concern rounding and improvement, rather than a promise that optimization always finds a global optimum.
neurips-2025-differentiable-extensions-w.tldr: Birkhoff Extension makes permutation objectives differentiable almost everywhere while guaranteeing that rounding does not worsen their value.

paragraphs: World models learn how an environment evolves so reinforcement learning agents can use experience more efficiently. One common approach compresses observations into discrete representations, which can discard visual details relevant to decisions. Diffusion-based alternatives improve visual fidelity, but conditioning predictions on a fixed number of recent frames restricts the history available to the model.

EDELINE addresses this memory problem by combining state space models with diffusion models in a unified architecture. The approach brings sequence modeling into the same world-model design as visual generation. Its motivation is to retain the benefits of detailed observation prediction while improving the ability to account for information beyond a short, fixed frame window.

The authors report better performance than existing baselines across visually challenging Atari 100k tasks, the memory-demanding Crafter benchmark, and first-person 3D ViZDoom environments. These evaluations test the architecture across different demands on perception and memory. The results support integrating temporal sequence modeling with diffusion-based world models as a way to improve reinforcement learning performance across the evaluated environments.
neurips-2025-edeline-enhancing-memory-in.tldr: EDELINE combines state space and diffusion models to strengthen world-model memory, outperforming baselines across three reinforcement learning benchmark settings.

paragraphs: Programming a language-model agent involves defining its workflow and deciding how it explores possible executions. Existing approaches often mix these responsibilities together. That coupling can make it awkward to experiment with inference-time methods such as tree search, because changing the search strategy also affects the code describing the agent’s task.

EnCompass introduces a programming model called probabilistic angelic nondeterminism to separate these concerns. Programmers describe the workflow, then choose inference-time strategies independently through a small set of inputs. The Python implementation uses a decorator to compile a workflow program into a search space, making possible execution paths available for the chosen search procedure.

Three case studies show that this organization lets programmers improve agent reliability and switch between inference-time strategies with little additional coding. The central contribution is therefore a programming abstraction that makes search easier to reuse and vary. The reported evidence demonstrates its usefulness in those case studies, while the broader design offers a way to explore agent execution strategies without repeatedly restructuring workflow logic.
neurips-2025-encompass-enhancing-agent-p.tldr: EnCompass compiles Python agent workflows into search spaces so developers can vary inference-time strategies with little extra code.

paragraphs: Flux4D reconstructs large dynamic scenes as three-dimensional structure that changes over time. Existing photorealistic reconstruction methods can face scaling difficulties and require annotations to separate moving actors. Other self-supervised approaches avoid explicit labels but still depend on optimizing each scene individually and can be sensitive to tuning.

The proposed framework directly predicts 3D Gaussians and their motion, using them to reconstruct sensor observations. Training combines photometric losses, which compare reconstructed appearance with observations, with an “as static as possible” preference. This regularization encourages a static explanation where possible while allowing motion to account for dynamic elements. Learning happens across many scenes without pretrained supervised models or foundation-model priors.

The authors report reconstruction within seconds and effective scaling to large datasets. Experiments on outdoor driving data show improvements over existing methods in reconstruction quality, scalability, and generalization. The system also generalizes to unseen environments containing rare or unknown objects. These findings support learning a reusable reconstruction model across scenes, with motion separation emerging from raw observations and the stated training constraints.
neurips-2025-flux4d-flow-based-unsupervi.tldr: Flux4D learns across scenes to predict 3D Gaussians and motion without annotations, enabling fast reconstruction of dynamic driving environments.

paragraphs: Segment Anything can generalize well on natural images yet make localized mistakes on medical structures such as blood vessels. Thin, complex shapes and unclear boundaries are especially challenging. FineSAM++ addresses these failures by adding targeted corrections to SAM’s segmentation outputs, concentrating its refinement effort on regions where structural uncertainty is high.

A confidence-driven soft routing module identifies those uncertain regions and activates a lightweight residual expert. The expert learns corrections to the existing prediction within the selected areas. This structure-aware, sparse expert design makes refinement selective: the added component focuses on local structural errors instead of treating every part of the image as equally in need of correction.

Experiments on five public vascular segmentation datasets show consistent improvements over both SAM-adapted baselines and task-specific models in accuracy and topological consistency. The latter concerns preservation of the predicted structure, beyond simply assigning pixels correctly. The findings support selective expert refinement as an effective way to improve foundation-model segmentations on the evaluated medical images, particularly where fine vessel structure is difficult to recover.
neurips-2025-gate-to-the-vessel-residual.tldr: FineSAM++ routes uncertain vessel regions to a lightweight correction expert, improving segmentation accuracy and structural consistency across five datasets.

paragraphs: A vision-language model can produce a convincing description that has little connection to the image it receives. This paper addresses that mismatch during decoding, when the model selects its response tokens. Its starting point is that strong language expectations can dominate visual evidence, allowing plausible wording to substitute for image-grounded content.

The proposed strategy uses conditional pointwise mutual information to strengthen the relationship between the generated text and the input image. It jointly considers textual and visual tokens through a bilevel optimization problem. A token purification mechanism selects text tokens that remain relevant to the image while refining the image tokens most pertinent to the developing response.

This two-sided adjustment matters because the method changes both what the model says and which visual information supports that response. Across multiple benchmarks, the authors report significant reductions in hallucinations while maintaining decoding efficiency. The findings support explicitly calibrating the relationship between visual and textual representations during generation as an effective way to reduce image-irrelevant responses in the evaluated models.
neurips-2025-grounding-language-with-vis.tldr: A mutual-information-based decoding method jointly refines visual and text tokens to reduce image-irrelevant responses while preserving decoding efficiency.

paragraphs: HCRMP investigates how language-model reasoning can assist reinforcement learning for driving without making control overly dependent on language-model outputs. The motivation is that erroneous semantic guidance can undermine a driving policy when the language model directly determines actions or gives decisive training instructions. The proposed framework instead treats its outputs as hints.

Those hints augment the agent’s state representation and assist policy optimization, while reinforcement learning can counteract incorrect guidance through learning. An augmented semantic representation module expands the available state information. A contextual stability anchor uses a knowledge base to improve the reliability of multi-critic weighting hints. A semantic cache connects infrequent language-model guidance with frequent control decisions.

In CARLA experiments, the authors report task success rates reaching 80.3% across driving conditions with different traffic densities. They also report an 11.4% collision-rate reduction in safety-critical conditions. These are simulation findings supporting the proposed division of responsibilities: semantic guidance provides context, while the reinforcement learning agent retains relative independence in learning its driving policy.
neurips-2025-hcrmp-an-llm-hinted-context.tldr: HCRMP uses language-model hints to support an independently learning driving policy, reporting improved success and fewer collisions in CARLA.

paragraphs: MATCH tackles semi-supervised segmentation of histopathology images, where densely packed objects make structural interpretation difficult. Unlabeled images can provide useful training information, but predictions may contain both meaningful structures and temporary artifacts. The framework focuses on preserving topological features that remain consistent across different predictions of the same data.

It produces varied predictions using stochastic dropout and model snapshots from different training times. Training then encourages agreement in their topological structure. A central difficulty is deciding which feature in one prediction corresponds to a feature in another when no ground-truth segmentation is available. MATCH addresses this with a matching strategy that combines spatial overlap and global structural alignment.

By establishing those correspondences, the method can reduce discrepancies across predictions and help separate persistent biological structure from noisy output. The authors report fewer topological errors and more accurate, robust segmentations in extensive experiments. The contribution makes structural consistency a source of supervision for unlabeled images, supporting the reliability of segmentations used in downstream histopathology analysis.
neurips-2025-match-multi-faceted-adaptiv.tldr: MATCH learns from unlabeled histopathology images by matching and preserving consistent topological features across varied predictions.

paragraphs: Recurrent networks can perform the same task equally well while implementing very different internal solutions. This solution degeneracy complicates attempts to infer a general computational mechanism by inspecting one trained network. The paper develops a unified framework for measuring and controlling variation in behavior, neural dynamics, and network weights.

The study examines 3,400 networks across four tasks: flip-flop memory, sine-wave generation, delayed discrimination, and path integration. It varies task complexity, learning regime, network size, and regularization. Greater task complexity and stronger feature learning reduce variation in neural dynamics but increase variation in weights, with mixed behavioral effects. Larger networks and structural regularization reduce variation at all three levels.

These empirical findings show why agreement at one level should not be treated as agreement at every level. Networks can become more similar in their evolving activity while becoming less similar in their parameters. The authors connect this pattern to the Contravariance Principle and provide guidance for tuning variability, whether the aim is to identify shared mechanisms or represent differences among biological systems.
neurips-2025-measuring-and-controlling-s.tldr: A study of 3,400 recurrent networks shows how training choices change solution variability differently across behavior, neural dynamics, and weights.

paragraphs: Novel class discovery for point-cloud segmentation asks a model to identify unlabeled 3D categories using supervision from labeled base categories. The challenge is to learn representations that connect points to known classes and support inference about unfamiliar ones. The authors argue that coarse statistical associations can create confusion when transferring between these groups.

Their method reformulates the task using a structural causal model. It analyzes hidden confounders in representations of base classes and relationships between base and novel classes. A causal representation prototype is designed to remove confounding influences and capture class-relevant representations. A graph then connects these base-class prototypes with novel-class prototypes, providing the structure for reasoning from known categories to new ones.

Experiments and visualizations on both 3D and 2D novel-class semantic segmentation show advantages for the proposed method. The results support the usefulness of combining representation learning with structured reasoning in these evaluations. The causal formulation supplies the method’s organizing constraints, directing learning toward class-related information and the relationships used to infer unlabeled categories.
neurips-2025-novel-class-discovery-for-p.tldr: The method combines causal class prototypes with graph-based reasoning to discover unlabeled segmentation categories from labeled base classes.

paragraphs: OmniGaze addresses poor transfer in 3D gaze estimation caused by limited and insufficiently diverse labeled data. It uses a large collection of unlabeled face images from unconstrained environments, covering variation in appearance, lighting, backgrounds, head orientation, and eye occlusion. The objective is to make this broader visual diversity useful for learning gaze direction.

The framework assigns pseudo-labels to unlabeled images and uses a reward model to estimate their reliability. That model considers the predicted 3D direction, visual embeddings from an existing encoder, and gaze-related semantic cues produced by a multimodal language model. Its confidence scores determine which pseudo-labels are retained and how strongly they contribute to the training loss.

The authors report state-of-the-art results on five datasets in both in-domain and cross-domain evaluations. They also demonstrate robust zero-shot generalization on four unseen datasets when evaluating the framework as a scalable data engine. These findings support confidence-based selection and weighting as a way to benefit from diverse unlabeled images while accounting for the varying quality of generated gaze labels.
neurips-2025-omnigaze-reward-inspired-ge.tldr: OmniGaze scores and weights pseudo-labels on diverse unlabeled face images to improve 3D gaze estimation across domains.

paragraphs: Unsupervised skill discovery aims to teach reinforcement learning agents varied behaviors without externally supplied rewards. Periodic Skill Discovery focuses on a particular kind of variety: repeated behaviors with different cycle lengths. This matters for robotic tasks such as locomotion, where useful behavior often involves recurring movement rather than simply reaching distinct states.

The framework trains an encoder to map states into a circular latent space. A circular representation naturally accommodates repetition, while information about temporal distance helps the method distinguish and learn skills with different periods. The authors show that this approach can discover periodic skills in complex robotic tasks, including settings where observations are images.

The learned skills achieve high performance on downstream tasks such as hurdling. Combining PSD with an existing skill-discovery method also produces more diverse behaviors. Together, these findings support explicitly representing periodicity as a useful complement to other discovery objectives. The contribution expands the kinds of behavior an agent can acquire, particularly when repeated motion at different timescales is important.
neurips-2025-periodic-skill-discovery-b8.tldr: Periodic Skill Discovery uses a circular latent representation to learn repeated robotic behaviors with diverse cycle lengths without external rewards.

paragraphs: PhysDiff detects anomalies in multivariate time series whose dynamics can change over time. Overlapping fast oscillations and slow trends make unusual behavior difficult to separate from normal variation. The method combines physics-guided signal decomposition with diffusion-based reconstruction, aiming to reduce interference between these components and make deviations easier to interpret.

An amplitude-sensitive permutation entropy criterion adaptively determines how deeply to decompose a signal. The resulting frequency components become explicit constraints for the diffusion model. A dual-path conditioning mechanism incorporates both high-frequency and low-frequency information, while time-frequency energy routing regulates denoising. The method then weights reconstruction errors across frequency bands to help localize anomalies.

Experiments cover five benchmark datasets and two NeurIPS-TS scenarios. The authors report outperforming 18 state-of-the-art baselines, including average F1-score improvements on standard and challenging datasets. These results support combining structured signal decomposition with learned reconstruction. The frequency-specific errors also give the approach a more interpretable basis for identifying deviations than an undifferentiated reconstruction discrepancy alone.
neurips-2025-physdiff-a-physically-guide.tldr: PhysDiff guides diffusion reconstruction with adaptive frequency components to improve time-series anomaly detection and interpretation.

paragraphs: Combining pretrained language models offers a way to bring together existing capabilities without training another model from scratch. A major obstacle is aligning the vocabularies of models with different architectures. Manually specified token correspondences can work unevenly across contexts, which the paper identifies as a source of degraded fusion performance.

PTA-LLM replaces rigid predefined alignment with a probabilistic, soft mapping. It formulates token alignment as an optimal transport problem, using information about distributions to establish correspondences. The central idea is to make vocabulary alignment sensitive to distributional structure, giving fusion a more general way to relate the tokens used by different models.

The distributional formulation also makes the alignment interpretable from the perspective of how those distributions are matched. Empirical evaluations show that the method improves the target model across multiple capabilities. These findings support token alignment as an important component of successful model fusion: improving the correspondence between vocabularies can help transfer capabilities more coherently, without requiring the abstract’s results to imply universal gains for every possible model combination.
neurips-2025-probabilistic-token-alignme.tldr: PTA-LLM uses optimal transport to learn soft vocabulary alignments, improving the evaluated target model across multiple capabilities.

paragraphs: Scientific literature tasks often require long-form synthesis rather than an answer that can be checked against one fixed solution. SciArena evaluates foundation models on these open-ended tasks through comparisons judged by researchers. Following an arena-style approach, it uses community votes to assess the quality of literature-grounded responses and build a model leaderboard.

At the point described in the paper, the platform supports 44 open-source and proprietary models and has collected more than 19,000 researcher votes across scientific domains. The authors analyze the collected data, report evidence of its high quality, and discuss insights from the resulting rankings. The platform makes researchers’ comparative judgments central to evaluation.

The paper also introduces SciArena-Eval, which uses those preferences to evaluate automated judges. A model’s pairwise answer assessments are compared with human votes to measure how well it reproduces researcher judgments. Experiments show that this is challenging, motivating more reliable automated evaluation. The two contributions therefore address both assessing scientific assistants and testing systems that would assess those assistants automatically.
neurips-2025-sciarena-an-open-evaluation.tldr: SciArena uses researcher preferences to evaluate literature-grounded model responses and to benchmark automated judges against human assessments.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning for language models usually updates the policy directly. ShiQ explores Q-learning, an alternative that learns values associated with choices and has advantages for sample-efficient and offline learning. Those properties are attractive when generating new language-model samples is computationally expensive, but straightforward Q-learning updates to token logits are ineffective.

The paper derives loss functions from Bellman equations while accounting for characteristics specific to language models. It interprets logits as Q-values and adapts the learning objective so those scores become reliable value estimates. These losses form Shifted-Q, or ShiQ, a practical algorithm supporting off-policy learning at the level of individual tokens.

Off-policy learning allows training to use experience beyond that produced by the currently updated policy, connecting the method to the motivation of making better use of available samples. Evaluations on synthetic data and real-world benchmarks, including UltraFeedback and BFCL-V3, demonstrate effectiveness in single-turn and multi-turn settings. The contribution is a theoretically grounded adaptation that makes Q-learning usable for language-model fine-tuning while remaining simple to implement.
neurips-2025-shiq-bringing-back-bellman-.tldr: ShiQ derives Bellman-based losses that turn language-model logits into useful Q-value estimates for off-policy, token-level learning.

paragraphs: Optimal transport finds a matching between distributions under constraints on their marginal probabilities. Semi-unbalanced transport relaxes one of those constraints, making matching more flexible. The paper focuses on formulations using KL divergence and addresses a concern with previous solvers: adding entropy regularization can lead to inaccurate matching solutions.

The proposed Equivalent Transformation Mechanism first determines the marginal probability distribution for the semi-unbalanced problem. The authors extend this approach to unbalanced optimal transport to examine its generality. Once the appropriate marginals are known, either problem can be transformed into a classical optimal transport problem, separating marginal determination from the subsequent matching step.

The paper also introduces a KKT-multiplier regularization term in combination with Multiplier Regularized Optimal Transport to improve matching accuracy. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods on the considered unbalanced and semi-unbalanced problems. The main contribution is a different computational route through these formulations: identify their marginals, recover a classical transport problem, and use the proposed regularization to obtain more accurate matches.
neurips-2025-solving-discrete-semi-unbal.tldr: The paper transforms KL-based unbalanced transport problems into classical transport after determining their marginals, then improves matching with multiplier regularization.

paragraphs: Sparse Gaussian processes use inducing points to make probabilistic modeling more computationally manageable. Recent methods improve these approximations by applying diagonal scaling to the conditional posterior given the inducing points. This paper replaces that diagonal structure with a block-diagonal one, allowing a richer structured approximation within the same broad framework.

The authors prove that the block-diagonal construction tightens the variational lower bound. This is a theoretical improvement in the approximation objective, distinct from an automatic guarantee about every prediction. They also revisit Power Expectation Propagation, showing how its unifying framework for sparse Gaussian processes can incorporate and benefit from these structured posterior approximations.

Across extensive regression experiments, the block-diagonal method performs similarly to or better than existing diagonal approximations while keeping computational costs comparable. The revised Power-EP framework is also competitive across different settings of its power hyperparameter. Together, these results offer practitioners a richer approximation without the reported experiments showing a corresponding increase in computational cost, alongside flexible alternatives to standard variational inference.
neurips-2025-sparse-gaussian-processes-s.tldr: Block-diagonal posterior approximations tighten a sparse Gaussian-process bound and match or improve regression performance at comparable computational cost.

paragraphs: HiMaCon aims to help robotic manipulation policies generalize by learning patterns of interaction that persist across tasks and environments. It learns these manipulation concepts from unlabeled multimodal data, avoiding human annotation. The representation is designed to capture both relationships among sensory signals and the different timescales over which actions unfold.

A cross-modal correlation network identifies persistent patterns shared across sensory modalities. A multi-horizon predictor then organizes representations at multiple temporal scales. These complementary components let a policy attend to transferable relationships while retaining information relevant to immediate actions and longer-term goals. The hierarchy therefore reflects temporal organization as well as common sensory structure.

The authors report significant performance improvements for concept-enhanced policies in simulated benchmarks and real-world deployments. Their analysis also finds that learned concepts resemble human-interpretable manipulation primitives despite the absence of semantic supervision. This suggests that useful, recognizable units of interaction can emerge from sensory correlations and temporal prediction. The findings support the proposed representation as a practical way to improve manipulation performance in the evaluated scenarios.
neurips-2025-textit-himacon-discovering-.tldr: HiMaCon learns hierarchical manipulation concepts from unlabeled sensory data, improving robotic policies in simulation and real-world deployments.

paragraphs: ToolRL studies how reinforcement learning rewards should be designed to teach language models tool use. Tool selection and application can involve several tools and varied parameters, making a single final-answer score an incomplete learning signal. The paper is motivated by difficulties supervised fine-tuning faces when tool-use situations become unfamiliar or complex.

The authors systematically examine reward types, scales, granularity, and how rewards change during training. They use those findings to develop a reward design tailored to tool-use tasks and train language models with reinforcement learning. The central emphasis is on the feedback supplied during learning, so that training can better distinguish the quality of tool choices and applications.

Across diverse benchmarks, the authors report robust, scalable, and stable training, with a 17% improvement over base models and a 15% gain over supervised fine-tuning models. These reported gains support the importance of reward design for tool-use capability and generalization. The study contributes both an investigation of reward-design choices and a training approach built from that investigation.
neurips-2025-toolrl-reward-is-all-tool-l.tldr: ToolRL systematically designs reinforcement learning rewards for tool use, reporting improvements over both base and supervised fine-tuned models.

paragraphs: Evidential deep learning represents uncertainty using Dirichlet distributions over class probabilities. This paper argues that training such models with completely certain hard labels creates a mismatch: the target provides no direct expression of ambiguity. The resulting distributions can become nearly deterministic, obscuring uncertainty from noisy data as well as uncertainty associated with the model.

The proposed approach replaces hard-label-only supervision with locally smoothed conditional label distributions through vicinal risk minimization. These richer targets expose the model to label uncertainty in a sample’s neighborhood. The aim is to better represent aleatoric uncertainty, which comes from data noise and ambiguity, while preventing distributional collapse that undermines epistemic uncertainty modeling.

Experiments compare the approach with standard evidential learning baselines on synthetic data, generalization under covariate shift, and out-of-distribution detection. The authors report consistently better performance and more reliable uncertainty estimates. The contribution places emphasis on the information supplied by training targets: uncertainty-aware outputs benefit from supervision that itself expresses local uncertainty, rather than asking the model to recover that uncertainty from fully certain labels.
neurips-2025-vicinal-label-supervision-f.tldr: Locally smoothed label distributions improve evidential models’ estimates of both data uncertainty and model uncertainty.
